body.title: withCacheIsolation declares a synchronous result but always returns a Promise
body.body:
Hullo folks,

I’m doing some research for Tessl Code Review and ran it against your repo. It flagged a potential issue, and I figured it made sense to share it with you:

## Describe the bug

`withCacheIsolation` is exported with return type `T`, but its implementation is always async. For a synchronous handler returning `Response`, the public type therefore permits `result.status` and `result.headers.get(...)`, while the actual result is a Promise. The first access returns undefined and the second throws.

Expected: the wrapper’s call signature exposes `Promise<Awaited<ReturnType<T>>>` (while retaining applicable copied properties), so TypeScript requires awaiting this result. Normal H3 route dispatch already awaits handlers; this report concerns direct consumers of the public helper.

## Environment

Current main: 2f29b875617e8daf39d25118f7474fd4c24fbfe1 (package.json: h3 2.0.8), Node.js 25.2.0, macOS 27.2 arm64. Executed the current source with srvx 1.0.6; no HTTP server or external service required.

## Reproduction

In a checkout of the commit above, with its runtime dependencies installed, save this as `repro.ts` at the repository root and run `node repro.ts`:

```ts
import { withCacheIsolation } from "./src/utils/cache.ts";
import { H3Event } from "./src/event.ts";

const event = new H3Event(new Request("https://example.test/"));
const result = withCacheIsolation(() => new Response("ok"))(event);
console.log(result instanceof Promise, result.status);
console.log((await result).status);
console.log(result.headers.get("content-type"));
```

The unwrapped handler returns a Response; awaiting the wrapped result also gives status 200. Direct access through the declared synchronous result fails.

## Logs

```text
true undefined
200
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')
```

## Additional context

This finding comes from [Simon’s retrospective Tessl review of merged PR #1608](https://github.com/sjmaple/cr-h3/pull/10#discussion_r4327620094), followed by the current-source reproduction above. It was also [flagged in the original upstream review](https://github.com/h3js/h3/pull/1608#discussion_r4326313968); I did not find a separate tracking issue or subsequent fix. This is a reproducible follow-up to that unresolved point, not a claim that it was first discovered here.

Validation was limited to the current helper and its actual event/dependencies under Node; I have not run the whole test matrix or proposed an implementation change.

Full transparency: I work at Tessl, and we've spotted that using Tessl Code Review -  using repository-level context and specific review lenses that improve over time through feedback. That’s how this finding surfaced.

We’re just getting started and want to offer the tool free to open-source projects. If this is useful, happy to give you access.

Bap

body.title: fix(types): emit declarations that typecheck with skipLibCheck: false
body.body:
Fixes #1657

### Summary

Downstream TypeScript projects importing `h3` with `skipLibCheck: false` failed `tsc --noEmit` unless they targeted `ESNext` and installed the optional peer dependency `crossws`:

1. `dist/h3.d.mts` emitted `static override isError` on `HTTPError`. Because `Error.isError` only exists in the `ESNext` lib, consumers targeting `ES2022` (or any pre-`ESNext` lib) got `TS4113`.
2. `dist/index.d.mts` imported `Hooks`, `Peer`, and `Message` from the optional peer `crossws`, producing `TS2307` when `crossws` is not installed.

### Changes

- Updated `build.config.ts` (`hooks.end`) to post-process emitted `dist/**/*.d.mts`:
  - Strip `override` from `static override isError` in published declarations while keeping `static override isError` in `src/error.ts` so this repo's own `noImplicitOverride` + `ESNext` typecheck continues to pass (`override` on `name` and `cause` stays intact because both exist in `ES2022`).
  - Prepend `// @ts-ignore optional peer dependency` above the `from "crossws"` import in `dist/index.d.mts`, suppressing `TS2307` when `crossws` is absent while preserving exact nominal types (`Peer`, `Message`, `Hooks`) when `crossws` is installed.
- Added a real `tsc --noEmit` consumer regression suite in `test/dts-consumer.test.ts` testing `skipLibCheck: false` + `noImplicitOverride: true` across `ES2022` and `ESNext`, both with and without `crossws` installed (and asserting nominal equality when `crossws` is present).

### Verification

- **Red before fix:** `pnpm exec vitest --run test/dts-consumer.test.ts` reproduced both `TS4113` (`h3.d.mts`) and `TS2307` (`index.d.mts`) on `ES2022` without `crossws`.
- **Green after fix:**
  - `pnpm build`
  - `pnpm lint` (`oxlint` + `oxfmt --check`)
  - `pnpm typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`)
  - `pnpm exec vitest --run test/dts-consumer.test.ts` — 4/4 passed.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved TypeScript compatibility for package declarations in downstream projects using ES2022 or ESNext, including setups with or without optional WebSocket support.
  * Corrected declaration compatibility for `HTTPError.isError`, helping consumers compile with strict library checking enabled.
  * These updates make it easier to use the package’s public types across different TypeScript configurations and optional dependency setups.

body.title: fix(handler): don't share pending load across lazy handler requests
body.body:
Fixes #1661

`defineLazyEventHandler` cached the first request's pending load promise and handed it to every later request. On Cloudflare Workers a promise can only settle in the request that created it, so if that first request is cancelled mid-load, the promise never settles and every later request to the route fails until the isolate is recycled. The same sharing also meant a rejected load was cached forever.

I changed it to cache only the resolved handler, as suggested in the issue. Until a handler has resolved, each request runs its own `loader()`. For `import()` loaders this is cheap since the module registry still evaluates the module once.

One behavior change: a loader that rejects is now retried on the next request instead of replaying the cached rejection.

Testing: added a regression test (first load never settles, second rejects, third succeeds). Before the fix it times out; after, `vitest run test/handler.test.ts test/lazy.test.ts` gives 40/40 passing. oxlint, oxfmt --check and tsc are clean.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed lazy-loaded handlers becoming unavailable after a load fails or remains pending. Subsequent requests can retry loading, and successful loads continue to serve later requests.
  * Improved recovery when a handler load returns an invalid result; the request receives an error instead of leaving the handler stuck in a failed state.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
